dutta-circle-task-local-minima: Section II, p.3: the authors state their own choice of the circle as test-bed boundary and why. Task design.
dutta-circuit-four-layers-ry-rz: Appendix A1, p.10-11: the circuit is stated as 4 layers, each Ul an Ry rotation then an Rz rotation. Own circuit design.
dutta-shots-per-point-150: Appendix A1, p.11, Step 6: Steps 3-5 repeated 150 times per training point; the later text says each point is iterated 150 times. Note: Section III, p.7 says 100 shots per measurement, an inconsistency inside the paper. The item records only what Appendix A1 states.
dutta-computational-cycle-definition: Section III, p.7: 'For the purposes of this study, we define a computational cycle...'. The paper defines its own term. Note it says 100 shots; Appendix A1 says 150 repeats.
dutta-ga-uncertainty-10-trials: Section II.A, p.3: the +/-2% error is stated as the standard deviation of 10 repeated trials on the same dataset. Own error-bar definition.
dutta-qpu-bfgs-step-05: Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 captions, p.5: BFGS finite difference with step size 0.5; the simulation was modified to the same step size to match the experiment. Own setup.
dutta-step-05-too-large: Appendix A4 5, p.28: the authors state two caveats on their own gradient experiment (gradient signs sometimes wrong; step 0.5 far too large). A limit on their own measured result; true type is measured/limit.
dutta-measurements-too-noisy-for-gradien: Appendix A4, p.25: 'We conclude that with our current NISQ setup, our measurements are too noisy to be used for gradient-based optimizers.' A limit the paper states on its own setup.
dutta-accuracy-cost-sparse: Appendix A3 2 a, p.18: follows directly from the accuracy cost defined in Eq. A2 (indicator of probability above 0.5); the paper states it as a caveat of that metric.
dutta-latency-bottleneck-limit: Section III, p.7: the paper states its own system's computation time is mainly limited by quantum-classical communication overhead and calls it a potential bottleneck. A limit on its own system.
setup-ion-trap-no-simulator: Intro p.1-2 and Section II p.3: ion-trap hybrid architecture, 250 random points in a 2D plane, training 'without the guidance of any classical simulation'. All stated by the paper as its own setup.
dzurak-paper-purpose-scope: Abstract, p.1: the paper states its own subject and main purpose.
dzurak-degree-structure-preserves-beng: Section II, p.2: the paper describes its degree structure, preserving UNSW BEng structure and inheriting electrical engineering courses.
dzurak-near-zero-background-assumed: Section III.A, p.3: stated course design assumption, with the reason (diverse cohort).
dzurak-students-write-simulation-code: Section III.A, p.3: stated teaching method; the passage names Matlab, switched to Python in 2021, and requires code from scratch.
dzurak-no-quantum-background-assumed-qco: Section III.B, p.4: the authors state the policy they adopted for the Quantum Communications course after the first lectures. Course design.
dzurak-qkd-half-the-course: Section III.B, p.5: 'Roughly half the course was spent on this application', then superdense coding and entanglement distribution, then elementary quantum error correction as third component. Own course content. (The third quote matches only after ligature normalization.)
dzurak-qcomms-open-challenges: Section III.B, p.5-6: the authors list remaining challenges of their own course (co-existence, duplication, single-photon focus).
dzurak-quantum-control-course-design: Section III.C, p.6: the authors describe their own course approach and the separation of filtering and control.
dzurak-qdc-course-content: Section III.D, p.6-7: the course follows Nielsen and Chuang, is system-agnostic, covers QFT, Grover, simulation, and an IBM Quantum Experience demonstration. Own course content.
dzurak-labs-qubitekk-and-nv: Section III.E, p.7: the paper states its own lab design. The kit description is the authors' account of their lab, not a measured claim.
dzurak-bb84-lab-no-secure-key: Section III.E, p.7-8: the authors state their own BB84 lab uses many-photon laser pulses and does not give an actual secured key. True type: setup with a stated limit.
egginger-setup-6-qubit-simulation: Section III-C, p.4: 5 dimensions, 6 qubits per Eq. (2), 200 datapoints or fewer, stated for compression due to simulation time.
egginger-models-svm-pennylane-simulators: Section III-A, p.3: sklearn SVMs with PennyLane quantum kernels on simulators.
egginger-binary-balanced-preprocessing: Section III-C, p.4: binary tasks, Fashion-MNIST T-shirt/Top and Dress, datasets balanced, features normalized, top 5 by ANOVA F-value. The balancing is in the passage though not in the quotes.
egginger-gd-outliers-removed: Section III-E, p.4: highest 3% of each GD removed for datasets 1 and 8; the near-singular matrix cause is stated as 'may occur'.
egginger-importance-method-gbdt: Section III-E, p.4: GBDT from sklearn fitted to the experimental data, Gini importance, C excluded from GD analysis because it does not affect the kernel.
egginger-relabel-method: Section III-D, p.4: lambda = 1.1, eigenvector of largest absolute eigenvalue, binarize at median, 5% set to 0. The purpose (favorable to quantum learners) is stated in the same passage.
egginger-insights-6-qubit-simulation-sco: Section V, p.7: the text layer interleaves two columns, but the sentence reads 'insights are specific to our experimental setup (6 qubits systems in a simulation environment, dataset preprocessed in the same way as outlined in Section III-C)'. The authors add a belief that they may hold more broadly; the value does not claim that.
egginger-future-noise-qubits: Section VII, p.10: the authors state noise and real hardware runs are not in this study and name them as future work. The 'may provide new insights' is hedged and stays hedged in the value.
ehrlich-vqe-definition-hybrid: Section I, p.2: the paper describes what VQE is (hybrid algorithm, parametrized trial state, classical minimization) for its readers. A description of the term, not a result; the 'significantly reduced depth' claim in quote 2 is not carried by the value.
ehrlich-tutorial-scope-newcomers: Section I, p.3: the paper states its own goal and audience, the per-section summaries and the two examples.
ehrlich-two-worked-examples: Section I, p.3: the paper states which two examples it covers (O2 in Sec. IV, Hubbard model in Sec. V).
ehrlich-vqe-building-blocks: Section II, p.3, Fig. 1: the paper lists the six components it treats as the essential building blocks of a VQE; this fixes the paper's own framework. All six bullets are in the passage though the quotes carry four.
ehrlich-table1-ansatz-scaling: Table I caption and legend, p.10: defines L, N, M, q and C and what the table summarizes. This grade covers the table's existence and notation only; the O() entries are cited scalings and are not settled by these quotes.
ehrlich-adapt-vqe-procedure: Section II.C.6, p.14: the paper spells out the ADAPT-VQE loop (pool, ranking metric, append, re-optimize, convergence exit) as its definition of the method. The method itself is credited to refs 130 and 131.
ehrlich-transpilation-definition: Section II.D, p.15: 'is called transpilation' defines the term.
ehrlich-bp-definition: Section II.G, p.21: 'This phenomenon is known as a barren plateau (BP)' defines the term as the paper uses it.
ehrlich-o2-setup-noiseless: Section IV, p.29: the paper states its O2 example is an idealized noiseless simulation with all-to-all connectivity, compared with CASCI. The 'upper bound' wording is the authors' framing of that setup.
ehrlich-o2-basis-active-space: Section IV.A-B, p.29-30: aug-cc-pVTZ, one-orbital entropy threshold 0.07, final (8,8) active space, triplet with five alpha and three beta electrons.
ehrlich-o2-ansatz-qubit-count: Section IV.C, p.30: UsCCSDTQ, Hartree-Fock initial state, Jordan-Wigner with symmetry reduction by two to four qubits, 12 qubits in some cases and one or two more in others. The paper's own computational setup.
ehrlich-o2-optimizer-simulator: Section IV.C, p.30: second-order Suzuki-Trotter, QuEST simulator, classically efficient gradient, scipy SLSQP.
ehrlich-hubbard-setup-6-site-12-qubits: Section V.B, p.32-33: 6-site chain at half-filling, 12 qubits, Jordan-Wigner, exact diagonalization reference, statevector simulator with COBYLA.
ehrlich-hubbard-hf-state-givens: Section V.B, p.33: the paper states it prepares the non-interacting ground state by Givens rotations ('as we do in the following'). The Slater-determinant fact is background and not a reason for LOW. The sentence is interleaved with a figure caption in the text layer but reads intact.
ehrlich-examples-no-noisy-hardware-run: Section IV, p.29 and Section V.B, p.33: the paper states both worked examples are noiseless simulations (idealized simulation; statevector, noise-free landscape).
vqe-review-scope: Abstract, p.1: the article states its own scope, a structured overview of VQE components and practical factors.
elyazizi-three-goals: Section 1, p.3-4: the paper states its first, second (hypothesis in two parts) and third goals. Own scope.
elyazizi-dataset-rbm-size: Section 3.2.1, p.9-10: OptDigits scaled to 8x8, ten one-hot label pixels, 74 visible units, 1,000 patterns, one CD step, aggressive L2 regularization to stay in the annealer's range.
elyazizi-hybrid-seed-procedure: Section 3.2.2, p.10-11: 1,000 anneals in a single job, 20 microsecond default time, majority vote, T = 0 relaxation, 500 target states, half of the seeds classical. Own protocol.
elyazizi-training-metrics-ais: Section 3.2.2, p.11: classification error and log-likelihood are the metrics; the partition function is estimated by AIS. The paper's own evaluation definition.
elyazizi-run-counts: Section 4.1, p.13-14: runs averaged over 10 (A, B) and only 3 (C) 'due to the limited D-Wave access time'; 1,000 samples each. A limit on its own hybrid experiment; true type is setup.
elyazizi-cf-protocol-setup: Section 3.3, p.11-12: Task-IL digit pairs for Tasks 1-5, 1,000 memories per class, Gibbs 200 k-steps at T = 1, one D-Wave call of 1,000 solutions with clamped labels and auto scaling off.
elyazizi-cf-scope-limit: Section 5, p.21-22: 'the focus was on a critical, but only one, aspect'; detection of when and which classes to generate was beyond the scope. A stated scope limit of the work.

theory_low.ehrlich-variational-principle: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section II, p.3: the ground state is the lowest-energy state by definition, but the inequality E0 <= <H> for any state and the variational principle are textbook results the paper states without proof.
theory_low.ehrlich-jordan-wigner-weight: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section II.B.1, p.7: the JW locality and parity statement and the largest Pauli weight are stated after Eqs. 8-10 without a proof.
theory_low.ehrlich-parity-mapping-saves-qubits: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section II.B.2, p.7: the Pauli weight similarity and one-qubit-per-sector elimination are argued in prose, not proved.
theory_low.ehrlich-ansatz-full-expressibility-param: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section II.C, p.8: a counting statement with no derivation. The text layer drops the superscripts, so '2M' means 2 to the power M; the parameter count is also not tied to real or complex parameters in the quote.
theory_low.ehrlich-cc-not-unitary-ucc: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section II.C.4, p.12: e^T is not unitary and e^(T-T dagger) is unitary because T-T dagger is anti-hermitian; stated in two sentences, and UCC is credited to the seminal VQE paper.
theory_low.ehrlich-shot-count-formula: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section II.E.1, p.17: Eq. 28 is given with refs 4, 5, 162 and no derivation. The text layer garbles the standard error (it should read sigma over the square root of S).
theory_low.ehrlich-hubbard-jw-ordering-pauli-weight: Section V.A, p.31: Pauli weights for a two-site Hubbard model read off Table III. A worked small case, not a stated and proved theorem; none of the five bases applies.
theory_low.ehrlich-hubbard-parity-mapping-weights: Section V.A, p.31-32: Pauli weights from Table III for a two-site model, and 'appears less favorable' for larger systems is not shown. A worked small case with an unproved extrapolation.
